did.abstract: John Ernest Merrill was born on May 9, 1872, in New York. His parents were George and Eunice Merrill. Isabel Trowbridge Merrill was born in London on August 12, 1876. Her parents were Tillman C. and Margaret Riggs Trowbridge. John and Isabel met while the two were in Aintab and would be married in 1905. They had two children, Dorothy and Margaret. Both John and Isabel were ABCFM missionaries in Turkey, specifically at the Central Turkey College. John would go on to be the president of the college and its successor, the Aleppo College in Syria while Isabel worked at the Girls' School in Aintab. They would leave the Middle East for the final time in 1936. Isabel died in Beacon, New York, on March 5, 1950, and John died in Bellows Falls, Vermont, on September 22, 1960. The collection contains records from John and Isabel Merrill, alongside other extended members of their family. This includes various diaries and journals, writings and reports, and letters.

bioghist.head: Biographical Information
bioghist.p: John Ernest Merrill was born on May 9, 1872, in New York. His parents were George and Eunice Merrill. He graduated from the University of Minnesota in 1891 and again in 1894 with his Ph.D. He would go on to graduate from the Hartford Theological Seminary in 1896 and then spend time at the University of Berlin. He died in Bellows Falls, Vermont, on September 22, 1960.

Isabel Trowbridge Merrill was born in London on August 12, 1876. Her parents were Tillman C. and Margaret Riggs Trowbridge. She went to Ferry Hall Seminary in Illinois and graduated from Vassar College in 1900. She died in Beacon, New York, on March 5, 1950.

Isabel grew up in Aintab as her father was the president of the Central Turkey College. He died when she was 12 and the family moved to Constantinople to be with her grandfather, Elias Riggs. She would attend the Women's College in Constantinople and was taught Greek by her grandfather. Following her time at Vassar, she took up a position at the Girls' School in Aintab where she met John.

John and Isabel were married in Switzerland on August 9, 1905. They had two children, Dorothy and Margaret. Both John and Isabel were ABCFM missionaries in Turkey, specifically at the Central Turkey College. Isabel, Margaret, and Dorothy would leave the country in May 1917, and John would not be able to join them in United States until the summer of 1920. John and Isabel returned to the Middle East in 1924 as John became the president of Aleppo College in Syria, the successor of the Central Turkey College. They would retire and leave for the United States in 1936.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains records from John and Isabel Merrill, alongside other extended members of their family. This includes various diaries and journals, writings and reports, and letters.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection has been arranged into three series, with each one being further arranged chronologically by start date.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: Additional letters by Isabel can be found in the "Vassar College Student Materials Collection, 1859-2025". Additional records from the Riggs family can be found from SALT Research based in Istanbul, Turkey.

corpname.part: American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains journals and diaries from John Merrill, Isabel Merrill and Isabel's mother Margaret Riggs Trowbridge.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains writings and reports, most attributed to John Merrill from his time working in Turkey as part of the American Commissioners for Foreign Missions. A large portion of these works related to the Central Turkey College and its successor, Aleppo College. Other material in the collection includes personal files between John and Isabel, a biography of Isabel Merrill by Dorothy Merill Dorman, and photographs.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains letters mostly written by John and Isabel Merrill to their daughters Margaret and Dorothy, but also to extended family and friends. The series also has letters by Isabel's father, Tillman C. Trowbridge and John Merrill's father, George Merrill. There are also letters from John Merrill that relate to his work through the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The letters were kept in the arrangement that they were received, with only slight edits to folder titles for readability.
